title: Bicycle

parts.label: Pedals
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the pedals do?
parts.explanation: When you push the pedals with your feet, you spin a toothed wheel. This is where all the force that moves the bike begins.

parts.label: Chain
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the chain does?
parts.explanation: The chain connects the pedals to the back wheel. When the pedal gear turns, the chain pulls another gear and spins the back wheel too.

parts.label: Wheels
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the wheels do?
parts.explanation: The wheels spin and roll along the ground, turning the force from your feet into forward movement.

parts.label: Brakes
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the brakes do?
parts.explanation: When you squeeze the levers, the brakes grip the wheels and make them stop spinning, so the bike slows down or stops.

summary: Now you know how it works! The pedals give force, the chain carries that force to the back wheel, the wheels spin forward, and the brakes stop everything when you need them to.

title: Car

parts.label: Engine
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the engine does?
parts.explanation: The engine burns fuel or uses electric energy to create force. It is the car's heart, making the energy that moves everything.

parts.label: Steering wheel
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the steering wheel does?
parts.explanation: The steering wheel is connected to the front wheels. When the driver turns it, the wheels turn that way and the car changes direction.

parts.label: Wheels
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the car's wheels do?
parts.explanation: The wheels get the force from the engine and spin on the road, making the car move forward.

parts.label: Brakes
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the car's brakes do?
parts.explanation: When the driver presses the brake pedal, discs squeeze the wheels tightly and the car slows down or stops.

summary: Now you know how it works! The engine makes the force, the steering wheel chooses the direction, the wheels carry the car forward, and the brakes stop everything safely.

title: Clock

parts.label: Battery
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the battery does?
parts.explanation: The battery gives electric energy to the clock, just like food gives energy to us. Without a battery, the clock stops.

parts.label: Gears
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the gears do?
parts.explanation: Gears are small toothed wheels inside the clock. Energy from the battery spins one, and it spins the next, always at the right pace.

parts.label: Hands
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the hands do?
parts.explanation: The hands are connected to the gears. They move slowly and precisely to show us the hours, minutes, and seconds.

parts.label: Dial
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the dial does?
parts.explanation: The dial has the numbers around it. It's where we read the position of the hands to know what time it is.

summary: Now you know how it works! The battery gives energy, the gears spin at the right pace, the hands move slowly, and the dial helps you read the time.

title: Smartphone

parts.label: Battery
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the battery does?
parts.explanation: The battery stores electric energy and powers every part of the phone, so it works even far from an outlet.

parts.label: Processor
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the processor does?
parts.explanation: The processor is like the phone's brain. It makes millions of calculations every second to open apps, games, and messages.

parts.label: Touchscreen
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the touchscreen does?
parts.explanation: The screen shows images and also senses your fingers touching it, so it knows where you want to tap and what to open.

parts.label: Antenna
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the antenna does?
parts.explanation: The antenna sends and receives invisible signals through the air, connecting the phone to the internet and letting you make calls.

summary: Now you know how it works! The battery gives energy, the processor thinks, the screen shows and senses touch, and the antenna connects the phone to the world.

title: Refrigerator

parts.label: Compressor
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the compressor does?
parts.explanation: The compressor is the fridge's engine. It squeezes a special gas, making it flow through pipes and become very cold.

parts.label: Refrigerant gas
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the refrigerant gas does?
parts.explanation: That cold gas flows through the walls inside the fridge and soaks up the heat from inside, keeping the food fresh.

parts.label: Thermostat
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the thermostat does?
parts.explanation: The thermostat is like a smart thermometer. It measures the temperature inside and turns the compressor on or off to keep it just right.

parts.label: Insulated door
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the insulated door does?
parts.explanation: The fridge's walls and door have a special material that stops the cold from escaping and the heat from getting in.

summary: Now you know how it works! The compressor moves the gas, the gas steals the heat from inside, the thermostat keeps the right temperature, and the insulated door keeps the cold in.

title: Elevator

parts.label: Buttons
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the buttons do?
parts.explanation: When you press a button, you tell the elevator which floor you want to go to. The system receives that request.

parts.label: Motor
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the elevator's motor does?
parts.explanation: The motor pulls the steel cables up or lets them slide down, making the cabin go up or down.

parts.label: Steel cables
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the steel cables do?
parts.explanation: The cables are very strong and hold up the cabin, connecting it to the motor above, so it never falls.

parts.label: Cabin
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the cabin does?
parts.explanation: The cabin is the box you step into. It slides along vertical rails and stops exactly at each floor's height.

summary: Now you know how it works! The buttons say which floor, the motor pulls the cables, the cables hold the cabin, and the cabin carries you right to the floor you chose.

title: Tap

parts.label: Water pipe
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the water pipe does?
parts.explanation: A pipe beneath the tap brings water from the house's pipes, always under pressure, waiting to come out.

parts.label: Valve
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the valve does?
parts.explanation: When you turn or lift the tap's handle, a valve inside opens a passage so water can flow through.

parts.label: Seal
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the seal does?
parts.explanation: A small rubber ring closes the gaps tightly, so the water only comes out the spout and doesn't drip elsewhere.

parts.label: Spout
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the spout does?
parts.explanation: The spout is the final exit. It's where the water leaves the tap, ready for you to wash your hands or fill a cup.

summary: Now you know how it works! The pipe brings the water, the valve opens the passage when you turn the tap, the seal stops leaks, and the spout lets the water out.

title: Toilet flush

parts.label: Flush button
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the flush button does?
parts.explanation: When you press the button, you open a valve inside the water tank that sits above or behind the toilet.

parts.label: Water flush
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think happens when the water rushes down?
parts.explanation: The water stored in the tank rushes down all at once with force, pushing everything in the bowl out through the drain pipe.

parts.label: Float
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the float does?
parts.explanation: After the flush, a float inside the tank rises slowly with the new water and, when it reaches the top, closes the valve that fills the tank.

parts.label: Trap
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the curved pipe does?
parts.explanation: The S-shaped pipe always holds a bit of water, creating a barrier that stops bad smells from rising up from the sewers.

summary: Now you know how it works! The button opens the valve, the water rushes down and cleans the bowl, the float refills the tank, and the trap holds water to block the smells.

title: Camera

parts.label: Lens
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the lens does?
parts.explanation: The lens is like a glass eye. It bends the light coming from the outside world and focuses it inside the camera.

parts.label: Shutter
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the shutter does?
parts.explanation: The shutter is a curtain that opens and closes very fast, letting light in for just an instant, the right time to take the picture.

parts.label: Sensor
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the sensor does?
parts.explanation: The sensor is inside and captures the light that passed through the lens, turning it into a digital image.

parts.label: Shutter button
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the shutter button does?
parts.explanation: When you press this button, you tell the camera the exact moment: open the shutter, let light in, and save the picture.

summary: Now you know how it works! The lens bends the light, the shutter opens for an instant, the sensor captures the image, and the button chooses the right moment to take the photo.

title: Solar panel

parts.label: Sunlight
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think happens when sunlight hits the panel?
parts.explanation: Sunlight is made of tiny packets of energy. When they hit the panel, that energy begins to be transformed.

parts.label: Solar cells
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the solar cells do?
parts.explanation: The cells are made of a special material that releases electrons and creates electricity when light hits it.

parts.label: Inverter
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the inverter does?
parts.explanation: The electricity that comes out of the panel isn't the right kind for the house. The inverter turns it into the kind of electricity we use in outlets.

parts.label: Wires
parts.predictionPrompt: What do you think the electric wires do?
parts.explanation: The wires carry the transformed electricity to the house, so you can turn on lights, watch TV, or charge your phone.

summary: Now you know how it works! Sunlight reaches the cells, the cells create electricity, the inverter turns it into the right kind, and the wires carry it to the house.
